output.analytic_position: This reading treats 'correction' strictly as the corpus's own correction field (a distinct event type, [correction], populated only in kind=changed-decision episodes), not as any inferred repair from failed or unknown tool results. The goal is to see what actually co-occurs with a recorded correction versus what does not, using only the frozen NUMBERED LINES as evidence. Tool failure and unknown status are treated as separate phenomena from human correction unless a correction line is also present in the same episode.

codes.interpretation: Correction in this corpus is recorded only when the human issues a new instruction that redirects target, scope, or visibility after the agent has already acted. It is a distinct line type ([correction]), not an inference from failure.

counterevidence.reason: E02 has a failed edit event but correction is null, showing tool failure alone does not produce a recorded correction.

codes.label: failed-tool-execution
codes.interpretation: Failed tool-result lines record an agent-side execution failure (wrong text match, patch rejection). In this frozen corpus these episodes never carry a correction line, so failure by itself is not treated as evidence of a required human correction.

counterevidence.reason: E04 shows a failed edit event co-occurring with a correction line, so failure and correction can appear together, weakening any claim that failure and correction are mutually exclusive.

codes.label: unresolved-tool-status
codes.interpretation: Unknown-status episodes lack any recorded tool result, so their outcome cannot be verified as succeeded or failed. None of these three episodes have a correction line, so 'unknown' is preserved as unresolved rather than upgraded or treated as a correction trigger.

counterevidence.reason: E12 has fully succeeded tool-result lines yet still carries a correction, showing that a clean unknown-free execution can still require correction, decoupling verifiable execution status from correction.

codes.label: clean-completion-no-correction
codes.interpretation: Episodes where every recorded event is succeeded and correction is null serve as the baseline: no redirection was needed when the agent's actions matched the request as given.

counterevidence.reason: E12 also has only succeeded tool-result events but still received a correction, showing succeeded-only execution does not guarantee correction-free episodes.

themes.name: Correction tracks human redirection, not tool outcome
themes.central_concept: In this corpus, the correction line appears only in changed-decision episodes, driven by the human restating target, scope, or visibility -- independent of whether the preceding tool events succeeded or failed.
themes.limits: Only three changed-decision episodes exist; the sample cannot establish that redirection is the only path to correction, only that it is the only path recorded here.

themes.name: Failure and unresolved status are preserved as distinct from correction
themes.central_concept: Failed and unknown tool-result lines describe execution-level problems (rejected patches, missing text, missing results) that are never, by themselves, accompanied by a correction line in this frozen corpus, so they must not be upgraded into 'required correction' claims.
themes.limits: E04 shows a failed event inside a correction-bearing episode, so failure and correction are not strictly disjoint categories; the theme describes a pattern in this sample, not a general rule.

questions_for_human: Should a correction be inferred when a failed or unknown tool-result line is never followed by any later succeeded event, even without an explicit [correction] line in this schema?
Is E04's co-occurrence of a failed edit and a correction evidence that failure caused the correction, or are these independent signals that happened to land in the same episode?
Should episodes with only unknown tool results (E03, E07, E11) be flagged as requiring correction due to unverifiable outcome, even though no correction line exists for them in this corpus?
